security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel sets the MTAG bit in a PTE for an executable page expecting that tag checks will be performed on loads/stores emitted by that code, but hardware (per the corrected spec) treats any page with MTAG+execute as 'tagcheck-exempt' — meaning loads/stores from that page skip tag checks entirely, silently defeating memory safety enforcement.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: PTE_MTAG set together with PTE_EXEC (pte_val() & (_PAGE_MTAG | _PAGE_EXEC)) == (_PAGE_MTAG | _PAGE_EXEC) without recognizing this creates a tagcheck-exempt page whose loads/stores bypass tag checks
security_spec.summary: Spec fix: MTAG+executable page is 'tagcheck-exempt' (loads/stores unchecked), not 'tagcheck-required' — kernel must not set MTAG on code pages expecting tag enforcement, or memory tagging silently degrades to no-op

findings.finding: The RISC-V Linux kernel defines no _PAGE_MTAG or equivalent memory-tagging PTE bit. The current PTE bits are: _PAGE_PRESENT(0), _PAGE_READ(1), _PAGE_WRITE(2), _PAGE_EXEC(3), _PAGE_USER(4), _PAGE_GLOBAL(5), _PAGE_ACCESSED(6), _PAGE_DIRTY(7), _PAGE_SOFT(8-9). No MTAG PTE bit exists to combine with _PAGE_EXEC, so the vulnerability pattern ((pte_val() & (_PAGE_MTAG | _PAGE_EXEC)) == (_PAGE_MTAG | _PAGE_EXEC)) cannot occur. The RISC-V Pointer Masking (Zpm) extension controls tag masking via CSR bits (menvcfg.PMM, senvcfg.PMM, mseccfg.PMM) rather than through PTE bits, and the spec explicitly states tag checks themselves are implementation-defined software or hardware features. The described MTAG+EXEC 'tagcheck-exempt' PTE behavior does not correspond to any ratified RISC-V extension or kernel implementation.

spec_citations.excerpt: The version of the extension being described here specifically targets **tag checks**: When an address is accessed, the tag stored in the masked bits can be compared against a range-based tag. [...] Pointer masking only adds the ability to ignore pointer tags during regular memory accesses. The tag checks themselves can be implemented in software or hardware.
